The World Bank Group’s Young Professionals Program is our flagship leadership development initiative, for highly talented individuals who are passionate about global development.
The Young Professionals Program offers a unique opportunity to build technical expertise, gain international experience, and contribute to projects that address the world’s most pressing development challenges.

Rotations provide participants with broad exposure to global operations and diverse development challenges, ensuring a well-rounded understanding of the institution’s work.
Beyond rotations, the program emphasizes continuous learning and career acceleration. Participants benefit from tailored leadership and technical training, dedicated mentorship, and direct engagement with senior leaders, creating opportunities to build strategic networks and gain insights into high-level decision-making.
Appointment Type:
GF-level term appointment
Duration & Contract:
The YPP is a 2-year program. Upon successful completion, participants are placed in a role for an additional 5 years based on performance, with the possibility of contract renewal.
YPP Tracks:
Candidates may apply under one of two tracks:
Operations
Specialized Functions
Rotations
The program includes three mandatory rotations of 8 months each, structured as follows:
One rotation within your primary function and area of expertise
One cross-institutional rotation
At least one rotation must be based in a country office

Education
Minimum graduate-level degree or a higher qualification in a relevant field, completed before September start date.
Experience
2 to 6 years of professional experience in the related work area. If you are pursuing a doctorate, full-time doctoral research studies in a relevant field at an accredited institution may count towards the required work experience, and the degree must be substantially complete with all the written work submitted before the September start date.
Language Proficiency
An excellent command of spoken and written English is mandatory. Fluency in additional languages is considered an advantage and may strengthen your application.
Employment Status
You cannot be a current World Bank Group employee at the time of application (including term, open, short-term [ST], and extended-term [ET] appointments). You also must not have a
close relative
working at the World Bank Group or a spouse in a
direct or indirect supervisory relationship

Is there an age requirement for the YPP?
There is no age requirement. Eligibility is based on the approved professional-experience requirement, not age.
I have less than 2 years or more than 6 years of experience, am I eligible to apply?
No, you must have at least two and no more than six years of qualifying full-time professional experience as of 1 Sep 2026.
Can a current or former World Bank Group staff or Independent Contractor (IC) apply?
If you have an active contract with the World Bank Group (WBG) as an Independent Contractor, you are not eligible for the YPP. Former WBG staff may apply if they otherwise meet the criteria, unless an applicable WBG policy, directive, or procedure states otherwise.
What is the date at which the years of experience are calculated?
Years of professional experience are calculated from the date of your earliest full-time professional experience after completing your undergraduate degree.
When should my term with the World Bank Group end to be eligible to apply?
You must not be a WBG Staff in Active Service at the time of your application.
What is the applicable employment eligibility policy?

. Some relationships may make an applicant ineligible; others may require safeguards concerning reporting lines, supervision, assignment, or routine professional contract. Review the official definitions and requirements before applying.
The stream I want to apply for is not listed. What can I do?
YPP streams reflect current WBG business needs and may vary by application cycle. If your preferred stream is not offered, apply only if another available stream genuinely matches your qualifications and career goals. You may also identify up to two additional streams for consideration within the same application.
What can I expect in the YPP application and selection process?
In the application, you will: select one primary stream and up to two optional alternatives; provide your contact information, education credentials, experience, and eligibility information; upload the required documents; and complete two written statements of up to 400 words each. Review the description and qualifications for each available stream before choosing.
What else should I expect to be able to respond to in my application?
Learn about the WBG mission, values, Scorecard, and the work of your selected stream. Review relevant projects, research, data, and strategy documents available through the WBG website. Focus on understanding the development challenges your stream addresses and how your experience could contribute.

The application form also includes two short written statements (up to 400 words each), where you can speak to both your general and stream-specific qualifications for the YPP. The prompts are designed to explore your motivation for joining us and to give us a sense of how you think about — and would approach — the challenges and opportunities central to our work and mission.
How should I decide which stream to apply for?
Choose the primary stream that most closely matches your education, technical expertise, and professional experience. Review the stream's work and qualifications and use the optional additional preferences only where your background credibly aligns.
I hear the program is competitive. What would increase my chances of success?
A strong application clearly demonstrates your fit with the selected stream. Use specific examples to show the depth of your technical expertise, the results of your work, how you approach complex problems, and how your conduct reflects WBG values. Answer the questions directly and accurately.

What is the selection process?
The selection process may include:
Eligibility and Application Review;
Asynchronous Video Interview,
Stream Specific Assessment and Virtual Job Try-out
Panel interview and Assessment Center
Final decision.
We will tell candidates in advance which stages apply to them.
Candidates advancing to the final stages are invited to a
panel interview
and
assessment center,
both conducted in person in December and January in Washington, DC, a country office, or online. The YPP team will work with invited candidates to plan and confirm interview dates and travel arrangements. Please note that attendance on the required dates is mandatory, and we are unable to reschedule or offer alternate dates. However, if you cannot attend on your assigned date, we will try our best to accommodate/offer alternate dates within the same interview period. In exceptional cases where dates cannot be accommodated and in-person travel is not possible, accommodations can be made for both the interview and the assessment center to take place online.
The panel interview lasts approximately 45 to 50 minutes and may include technical experts, senior WBG staff, and an HR representative. The assessment center includes a collaborative case exercise and a short, written reflection. Together, these activities assess technical depth and breadth, quantitative and qualitative thinking, problem-solving, communication ability, judgement, self-reflection, motivation, and alignment with WBG mission and values.
The assessment center takes approximately one hour and consists of a group exercise (around 45 minutes) based on a WBG case study, which ends with a joint presentation to a representative, followed by a written reflection (around 15 minutes). The group exercise assesses teamwork, communication, leadership skills, and WBG values, while the written reflection is used to evaluate concise written communication, business judgement, and self-reflection.
If I am invited to interview for the YPP, what should I do to prepare effectively?
You will be asked questions in your declared stream of technical specialty; experts in that stream will ask you about your work or a specific issue in that field, as well as related issues from the experts in other sectors. The interview helps us learn more about you, how you think, structure and solve problems, and assess your technical depth and breadth. We may ask you additional questions, such as the ones that help us assess your comfort with our ethical principles and shared values.
What can I bring for the interview?
title: World Bank Group Young Professionals Program

text:
What can I bring for the interview?
Follow the instructions in your interview invitation. For an in-person interview, bring the requested identification and materials (national ID for verification purposes and laptop). For an online interview, test your connection and equipment in advance. Unless instructed otherwise, do not consult prepared notes or outside sources during the interview.
When are the offers issued?
Prospective Young Professionals (YPs) will be informed of hiring decisions in late January or early February.
Can I negotiate my salary and benefits?
No. YPP salary and benefits are determined using established WBG criteria and are not individually negotiated. Your offer letter will provide the details applicable to your appointment.
I am a non-U.S. citizen; will my spouse get a dependent visa if I am hired as a Young Professional?
Yes, spouses and dependents of WBG staff are eligible to apply for G-4 Dependent Visas.
I am a domestic partner (not legally married), will I get a dependent visa if my spouse is accepted as a Young Professional?
For purposes of G-4 visa eligibility, the U.S. Department of State recognizes only legally married spouses. Accordingly, domestic partners, regardless of whether the relationship is same-sex or opposite-sex, do not qualify for G-4 dependent status.
Can I apply again if I have applied before?
You are welcome to reapply if you meet the eligibility criteria. You might want to assess whether your application is likely to be competitive by ensuring that you have continued to develop professionally since the previous application. We do not advise reusing your prior responses (particularly if the prompts in the application form have changed).
Can I apply to more than one position?
No. Applicants may submit only one application to the Young Professionals Program. As part of your application, you may indicate up to two additional streams for consideration if your profile aligns with the requirements.
Please note that submitting more than one application will result in disqualification.
If my application is successful, can I defer my start date?
No, the YPP includes cohort-based participation and learning that is core to the program. We do not defer the start date.
Can I choose my location during the YPP?
All WBG YPs start their assignments at the World Bank Group headquarters in Washington, DC. Rotation locations are determined by program requirements, business needs and development objectives; at least one rotation is based in a country offices.
Would you accept a late application?
No, please plan to apply in advance of the deadline as no late submissions, applications submitted by email, or changes to the application will be accepted after the deadline.
What happens if I am not selected?
There are other ways to join the World Bank Group. Please visit our main
Careers
page to learn more and see open positions.

Why am I not receiving status updates about my application?
In order to receive status updates about your application in your inbox, please ensure that you sign up for an account on the WBG Careers website in addition to submitting your application. Status updates will also be available under the specific requisition you have applied for on the WBG Careers website.
